definition: The named EquineSync Founder or a successor authority designated by durable governing record within the scope of that designation.
Written, scoped authority granted by the Founder or competent governing instrument; it cannot expand itself.
Repository-native or otherwise preserved record with date, scope, authority, hash or exact identity where applicable, and retention treatment.
Capable of changing authority, lifecycle state, evidence sufficiency, risk, privacy, security, safeguarding, financial, production, or implementation effect.
Administrative, editorial, or clarifying change that does not alter authority, evidence, risk, scope, or obligations.
No more governance burden than needed to preserve truthful evidence and control the affected risk class.
A control burden materially exceeding the risk or authority consequence when a truthful lighter control would suffice.
Acceptable for the bounded continuation purpose based on named evidence, known limitations, and retained defects; not a claim of independent verification.
Event that may affect security, privacy, safeguarding, financial integrity, availability, evidence integrity, or authority validity.
Founder, delegated authority, or governing body with written scope covering the decision.
Commit, protected branch head, tag, or release reference subject to repository controls and recorded exact identity.
The precise byte sequence of a source file or package with SHA-256 and byte length recorded.
Checked against running code or implementation artifacts by an executed method recorded with evidence.
Observed in production or production-equivalent environment with environment, time, scope, and evidence recorded.
Known risk accepted by competent authority with owner, scope, controls, review date, and consequences.
Time-limited authorization to proceed without a required test or control; it cannot be permanent and cannot turn an unexecuted check into PASS.
Bounded departure from a default governance requirement recorded with scope, duration, authority, limits, and review trigger.
Authorized replacement of required evidence with alternative evidence and limitations.
Procedural bypass of an internal gate by competent authority, excluding the non-waivable core.
Durable record ending or withdrawing a prior authority, certification, waiver, substitution, or override.
Temporary halt or qualification of an authority or claim pending review.
Bounded conclusion that specified criteria are satisfied or dispositioned with retained limitations, authority, and reopening triggers recorded.
